spec.title: OpenWrt - NetFlow
spec.description: Per-flow traffic from softflowd via Akvorado, stored in ClickHouse, plus the exporter and collector health that says whether it is complete.

options.content:
## Per-flow traffic
NetFlow v9 from softflowd on the router, collected by Akvorado and stored in ClickHouse. Byte counts are multiplied by the reported sampling rate.

**Coverage caveat:** softflowd captures with libpcap, so traffic forwarded by the switch ASIC under hardware flow offload never reaches it. Check the **Pipeline Health** tab before treating these totals as complete.

spec.title: Flows
spec.description: Flow records stored in the selected range.

spec.rawSql: SELECT count() AS flows FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router)

spec.title: Traffic
spec.description: Total bytes in the selected range, sampling-rate corrected.

spec.rawSql: SELECT sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS bytes FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router)

spec.title: Peak Bitrate
spec.description: Highest sampling-rate-corrected bitrate bucket in the selected range.

spec.rawSql: SELECT max(bps) AS bps FROM (SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeReceived) AS time, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) * 8 / $__interval_s AS bps FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) GROUP BY time)

spec.title: External Share
spec.description: Share of bytes that cross the local network boundary rather than staying LAN-local. On a typical home network this is low -- most bytes are between local devices -- which is the context every other panel on this dashboard should be read in. Derived from address role, not interface boundary.

spec.rawSql: SELECT round(100 * sumIf(Bytes * SamplingRate, (SrcNetRole != 'internal' OR DstNetRole != 'internal')) / greatest(sum(Bytes * SamplingRate), 1)) AS pct FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router)

spec.title: IPv6 Flow Share
spec.description:
Share of flow records carried over IPv6, from the ethertype.

This is a share of **flows**, not of bytes. The two differ sharply here: IPv6 carries a meaningful fraction of conversations (DNS, mDNS, NTP, service discovery) while the large transfers are still IPv4, so byte share reads near zero and would look like an enrichment failure rather than a real property of the traffic.

spec.rawSql: SELECT round(100 * countIf(EType = 34525) / greatest(count(), 1)) AS pct FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router)

spec.title: Local Hosts
spec.description: Distinct local source addresses seen. Depends on the `networks` prefixes in akvorado.yaml matching your addressing.

spec.rawSql: SELECT uniq(SrcAddr) AS hosts FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND SrcNetRole = 'internal'

spec.title: External Peers
spec.description: Distinct internet-side addresses contacted.

spec.rawSql: SELECT uniq(DstAddr) AS peers FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND DstNetRole != 'internal'

spec.title: ASN Coverage
spec.description: Share of boundary-crossing flows with a source or destination AS after GeoIP/ASN enrichment.

spec.rawSql: SELECT round(100 * countIf(SrcAS != 0 OR DstAS != 0) / greatest(count(), 1)) AS pct FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND (SrcNetRole != 'internal' OR DstNetRole != 'internal')

spec.title: Peak Link Utilization
spec.description:
Peak bitrate as a fraction of the capture interface's reported link speed (InIfSpeed, a constant 1 Gbps here).

This is a **lower bound**: anything hardware flow offload hid from softflowd is missing from the numerator, so real link utilization is at least this high. Use it for 'is the link anywhere near saturated', not for capacity planning.

spec.rawSql: SELECT max(bps) / greatest(max(link_bps), 1) AS util FROM (SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeReceived) AS time, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) * 8 / $__interval_s AS bps, max(InIfSpeed) * 1000000 AS link_bps FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) GROUP BY time)

spec.title: Throughput by Direction
spec.description:
Bit rate split into outbound, inbound, and LAN-local, derived from whether each address falls in one of the `clickhouse.networks` prefixes in akvorado.yaml.

This deliberately does NOT use InIfBoundary: softflowd reports the same ifIndex for both ingress and egress, so interface boundary is constant across every flow and cannot distinguish direction. If everything lands in one series, your LAN prefix is missing from `clickhouse.networks`.

spec.rawSql: SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeReceived) AS time, sumIf(Bytes * SamplingRate * 8 / $__interval_s, multiIf(SrcNetRole = 'internal' AND DstNetRole = 'internal', 'local', SrcNetRole = 'internal', 'outbound', 'inbound') = 'outbound') AS "outbound", sumIf(Bytes * SamplingRate * 8 / $__interval_s, multiIf(SrcNetRole = 'internal' AND DstNetRole = 'internal', 'local', SrcNetRole = 'internal', 'outbound', 'inbound') = 'inbound') AS "inbound", sumIf(Bytes * SamplingRate * 8 / $__interval_s, multiIf(SrcNetRole = 'internal' AND DstNetRole = 'internal', 'local', SrcNetRole = 'internal', 'outbound', 'inbound') = 'local') AS "local" FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

spec.title: Direction Share
spec.description: The same three buckets as the panel on the left, stacked to 100%. This answers 'what is the mix right now' rather than 'how much is there' -- useful for spotting a shift to outbound traffic that the absolute view hides because the total barely moved.

spec.rawSql: SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeReceived) AS time, sumIf(Bytes * SamplingRate, multiIf(SrcNetRole = 'internal' AND DstNetRole = 'internal', 'local', SrcNetRole = 'internal', 'outbound', 'inbound') = 'outbound') AS "outbound", sumIf(Bytes * SamplingRate, multiIf(SrcNetRole = 'internal' AND DstNetRole = 'internal', 'local', SrcNetRole = 'internal', 'outbound', 'inbound') = 'inbound') AS "inbound", sumIf(Bytes * SamplingRate, multiIf(SrcNetRole = 'internal' AND DstNetRole = 'internal', 'local', SrcNetRole = 'internal', 'outbound', 'inbound') = 'local') AS "local" FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

spec.title: Top Local Talkers
spec.description: Busiest local sources by uploaded bytes. Raw `flows` table only, so bounded by the interval-0 retention window.

spec.rawSql: SELECT replaceRegexpAll(IPv6NumToString(SrcAddr), '^::ffff:', '') AS host, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS bytes FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND SrcNetRole = 'internal' GROUP BY host ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 15

spec.title: Top External Destinations
spec.description: Busiest internet-side destinations by bytes.

spec.rawSql: SELECT replaceRegexpAll(IPv6NumToString(DstAddr), '^::ffff:', '') AS peer, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS bytes FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND DstNetRole != 'internal' GROUP BY peer ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 15

spec.title: Top Conversations
spec.description: Individual source/destination/port conversations, heaviest first. This is the panel that answers 'what is saturating the link right now'.

spec.rawSql: SELECT replaceRegexpAll(IPv6NumToString(SrcAddr), '^::ffff:', '') AS Source, replaceRegexpAll(IPv6NumToString(DstAddr), '^::ffff:', '') AS Destination, DstPort AS Port, dictGetOrDefault('protocols', 'name', toUInt64(Proto), toString(Proto)) AS Protocol, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS Bytes, sum(Packets * SamplingRate) AS Packets FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) GROUP BY Source, Destination, Port, Protocol ORDER BY Bytes DESC LIMIT 50

options.content:
## Ports and protocols
Port numbers are a weak proxy for application identity -- almost everything is 443/TCP now. For real application labels, install the `dpi` profile (Netifyd) and use the Advanced dashboard; this tab answers 'which service ports and protocols carry the bytes', not 'which app'.

spec.title: Top Destination Ports
spec.description: Internet-side destination ports by bytes. This is usually the most useful port ranking for web, DNS, streaming, VPN, and gaming traffic.

spec.rawSql: SELECT concat(toString(DstPort), '/', dictGetOrDefault('protocols', 'name', toUInt64(Proto), toString(Proto))) AS port, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS bytes FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND DstNetRole != 'internal' GROUP BY port ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 15

spec.title: Top Source Ports
spec.description: Source ports by bytes. Expect many ephemeral client ports here; fixed source ports such as 443/UDP or 9100/TCP are the interesting exceptions.

spec.rawSql: SELECT concat(toString(SrcPort), '/', dictGetOrDefault('protocols', 'name', toUInt64(Proto), toString(Proto))) AS port, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS bytes FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND SrcPort > 0 GROUP BY port ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 15

spec.title: Protocol Mix
spec.description: Share of bytes by IP protocol.

spec.rawSql: SELECT dictGetOrDefault('protocols', 'name', toUInt64(Proto), toString(Proto)) AS protocol, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS bytes FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) GROUP BY protocol ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 10

spec.title: Throughput by Destination Port
spec.description: Bit rate over time for the eight busiest destination ports in the range.

spec.rawSql: SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeReceived) AS time, toString(DstPort) AS port, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) * 8 / $__interval_s AS bps FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND DstNetRole != 'internal' AND DstPort IN (SELECT DstPort FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND DstNetRole != 'internal' GROUP BY DstPort ORDER BY sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) DESC LIMIT 8) GROUP BY time, port ORDER BY time

spec.title: Service Class Mix
spec.description: Human-readable service buckets from source and destination ports. This is a convenience grouping, not DPI. Answers 'what is the mix over the whole range'; the companion panel below answers 'did it change'.

spec.rawSql: SELECT multiIf(DstPort IN (53, 853) OR SrcPort IN (53, 853), 'DNS / encrypted DNS', DstPort IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443) OR SrcPort IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443), 'Web / QUIC', DstPort IN (9100, 9090, 3000, 8081, 8123) OR SrcPort IN (9100, 9090, 3000, 8081, 8123), 'Monitoring stack', DstPort IN (22, 2222) OR SrcPort IN (22, 2222), 'SSH / admin', DstPort = 123 OR SrcPort = 123, 'NTP', DstPort = 5353 OR SrcPort = 5353, 'mDNS', DstPort = 1900 OR SrcPort = 1900, 'SSDP / discovery', 'Other') AS service, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS bytes FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) GROUP BY service ORDER BY bytes DESC

spec.title: Packet Size over Time
spec.description:
Packets per mean-packet-size bucket, over time. Column names are bucket **upper** bounds in bytes.

A band that sits at the bottom is interactive, control, and ACK traffic; weight in the 1024-1500 band is bulk transfer. The shift between them across a day is the shape worth watching -- a sustained small-packet band alongside a high flow count is also what scan-like behaviour looks like.

Sizes are per-flow means (`PacketSize`), not per-packet, so a flow mixing large and tiny packets lands in a middle bucket rather than in both.

spec.rawSql: SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeReceived) AS time, sumIf(Packets * SamplingRate, PacketSize < 64) AS "64", sumIf(Packets * SamplingRate, PacketSize >= 64 AND PacketSize < 128) AS "128", sumIf(Packets * SamplingRate, PacketSize >= 128 AND PacketSize < 256) AS "256", sumIf(Packets * SamplingRate, PacketSize >= 256 AND PacketSize < 512) AS "512", sumIf(Packets * SamplingRate, PacketSize >= 512 AND PacketSize < 1024) AS "1024", sumIf(Packets * SamplingRate, PacketSize >= 1024 AND PacketSize < 1500) AS "1500", sumIf(Packets * SamplingRate, PacketSize >= 1500) AS "+Inf" FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

spec.title: TCP Flow Outcomes
spec.description:
TCP flag bitmasks decoded into what actually happened to each flow.

`TCPFlags` is the cumulative OR of every packet's flags across the flow's lifetime, so it describes an outcome rather than a packet: a flow carrying both SYN and FIN was opened and closed inside the capture window.

- **Completed** -- handshake and close both seen. The healthy majority.
- **RST** -- something reset the connection. Normal in small amounts (browsers abandon connections constantly); a sustained rise against one destination is a service refusing.
- **SYN, never answered** -- a connection attempt that got nothing back. This is the scan and unreachable-host signature, and it is normally near zero here.
- **Open / Established** -- still running when the flow was cut. Expected, because `maxlife=60` cuts every flow once a minute regardless of state.

Colours are an identity contract shared with the Security Signals tab.

spec.rawSql: SELECT multiIf(bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0 AND bitAnd(TCPFlags, 16) = 0, 'SYN, never answered', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 4) != 0, 'RST - reset or refused', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 1) != 0 AND bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0, 'Completed - opened and closed', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 1) != 0, 'Closed - handshake not captured', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0, 'Open - handshake, still running', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 16) != 0, 'Established - data only', 'Other') AS shape, count() AS flows FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND Proto = 6 GROUP BY shape ORDER BY flows DESC

spec.title: Top Local Service Ports
spec.description: Ports receiving traffic on internal destinations. Useful for spotting local scrapes, media servers, admin interfaces, and noisy LAN services.

spec.rawSql: SELECT concat(toString(DstPort), '/', dictGetOrDefault('protocols', 'name', toUInt64(Proto), toString(Proto))) AS port, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS bytes FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND DstNetRole = 'internal' AND DstPort > 0 GROUP BY port ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 15

spec.title: Port Conversation Matrix
spec.description: Source-to-destination port pairs. This makes fixed source-port services stand out from ordinary client ephemeral ports.

spec.rawSql: SELECT concat(toString(SrcPort), ' -> ', toString(DstPort), '/', dictGetOrDefault('protocols', 'name', toUInt64(Proto), toString(Proto))) AS PortPath, count() AS Flows, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS Bytes, sum(Packets * SamplingRate) AS Packets FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND SrcPort > 0 AND DstPort > 0 GROUP BY PortPath ORDER BY Bytes DESC LIMIT 40

spec.title: Service Class over Time
spec.description:
The same port-derived service buckets as the donut above, stacked to 100% over time.

Read it for shape changes rather than for levels: a backup window, a streaming session, or an overnight update run all show up here as one band taking over, where the donut would only show a slightly different slice.

spec.rawSql: SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeReceived) AS time, sumIf(Bytes * SamplingRate, multiIf(DstPort IN (53, 853) OR SrcPort IN (53, 853), 'DNS / encrypted DNS', DstPort IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443) OR SrcPort IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443), 'Web / QUIC', DstPort IN (9100, 9090, 3000, 8081, 8123) OR SrcPort IN (9100, 9090, 3000, 8081, 8123), 'Monitoring stack', DstPort IN (22, 2222) OR SrcPort IN (22, 2222), 'SSH / admin', DstPort = 123 OR SrcPort = 123, 'NTP', DstPort = 5353 OR SrcPort = 5353, 'mDNS', DstPort = 1900 OR SrcPort = 1900, 'SSDP / discovery', 'Other') = 'DNS / encrypted DNS') AS "DNS / encrypted DNS", sumIf(Bytes * SamplingRate, multiIf(DstPort IN (53, 853) OR SrcPort IN (53, 853), 'DNS / encrypted DNS', DstPort IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443) OR SrcPort IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443), 'Web / QUIC', DstPort IN (9100, 9090, 3000, 8081, 8123) OR SrcPort IN (9100, 9090, 3000, 8081, 8123), 'Monitoring stack', DstPort IN (22, 2222) OR SrcPort IN (22, 2222), 'SSH / admin', DstPort = 123 OR SrcPort = 123, 'NTP', DstPort = 5353 OR SrcPort = 5353, 'mDNS', DstPort = 1900 OR SrcPort = 1900, 'SSDP / discovery', 'Other') = 'Web / QUIC') AS "Web / QUIC", sumIf(Bytes * SamplingRate, multiIf(DstPort IN (53, 853) OR SrcPort IN (53, 853), 'DNS / encrypted DNS', DstPort IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443) OR SrcPort IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443), 'Web / QUIC', DstPort IN (9100, 9090, 3000, 8081, = 5353, 'mDNS', DstPort = 1900 OR SrcPort = 1900, 'SSDP / discovery', 'Other') = 'Monitoring stack') AS "Monitoring stack", sumIf(Bytes * SamplingRate, multiIf(DstPort IN (53, 853) OR SrcPort IN (53, 853), 'DNS / encrypted DNS', DstPort IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443) OR SrcPort IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443), 'Web / QUIC', DstPort IN (9100, 9090, 3000, 8081, 8123) OR SrcPort IN (9100, 9090, 3000, 8081, 8123), 'Monitoring stack', DstPort IN (22, 2222) OR SrcPort IN (22, 2222), 'SSH / admin', DstPort = 123 OR SrcPort = 123, 'NTP', DstPort = 5353 OR SrcPort = 5353, 'mDNS', DstPort = 1900 OR SrcPort = 1900, 'SSDP / discovery', 'Other') = 'SSH / admin') AS "SSH / admin", sumIf(Bytes * SamplingRate, multiIf(DstPort IN (53, 853) OR SrcPort IN (53, 853), 'DNS / encrypted DNS', DstPort IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443) OR SrcPort IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443), 'Web / QUIC', DstPort IN (9100, 9090, 3000, 8081, 8123) OR SrcPort IN (9100, 9090, 3000, 8081, 8123), 'Monitoring stack', DstPort IN (22, 2222) OR SrcPort IN sumIf(Bytes * SamplingRate, multiIf(DstPort IN (53, 853) OR SrcPort IN (53, 853), 'DNS / encrypted DNS', DstPort IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443) OR SrcPort IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443), 'Web / QUIC', DstPort IN (9100, 9090, 3000, 8081, 8123) OR SrcPort IN (9100, 9090, 3000, 8081, 8123), 'Monitoring stack', DstPort IN (22, 2222) OR SrcPort IN (22, 2222), 'SSH / admin', DstPort = 123 OR SrcPort = 123, 'NTP', DstPort = 5353 OR SrcPort = 5353, 'mDNS', DstPort = 1900 OR SrcPort = 1900, 'SSDP / discovery', 'Other') = 'mDNS') AS "mDNS", sumIf(Bytes * SamplingRate, multiIf(DstPort IN (53, 853) OR SrcPort IN (53, 853), 'DNS / encrypted DNS', DstPort IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443) OR SrcPort IN (80, 443, 8080, 8443), 'Web / QUIC', DstPort IN (9100, 9090, 3000, 8081, 8123) OR SrcPort IN (9100, 9090, 3000, 8081, 8123), 'Monitoring stack', DstPort IN (22, 2222) OR SrcPort IN (22, 2222), 'SSH / admin', DstPort = 123 OR SrcPort = 123, 'NTP', DstPort = 5353 OR SrcPort = 5353, 'mDNS', DstPort = 1900 OR SrcPort = "Other" FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

options.content:
## Autonomous systems and geography
ASN and country enrichment comes from the MaxMind/IPinfo databases mounted in `akvorado/geoip/`. When the databases are missing, Akvorado still stores flows but AS, country, and network labels stay empty. The resolution tiles below make that state explicit.

**Resolution here reads low by design, and that is not a fault.** Most flows on this network are LAN-to-LAN, and a private address has no AS or country by definition. The tiles measure resolution over boundary-crossing flows, so the honest reading is 'of the traffic that actually left, how much did we identify' -- not 'how much of the enrichment is broken'.

Read source-side panels as **who sent traffic to you or to local services** and destination-side panels as **where your clients sent traffic**. On a home LAN most source ports are ephemeral; AS and destination ports are usually the cleaner story.

City-level enrichment is deliberately off (the City and Country databases together OOM the orchestrator at its current memory limit), so there is no city panel here.

spec.title: Destination AS Resolution
spec.description: Share of outbound/external-destination flows that resolved to a destination AS number.

spec.rawSql: SELECT round(100 * countIf(DstAS != 0) / greatest(count(), 1)) AS pct FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND DstNetRole != 'internal'

spec.title: Source AS Resolution
spec.description: Share of internet-source flows that resolved to a source AS number.

spec.rawSql: SELECT round(100 * countIf(SrcAS != 0) / greatest(count(), 1)) AS pct FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND SrcNetRole != 'internal'

spec.title: Country Resolution
spec.description: Share of boundary-crossing flows with either side resolved to a non-empty country code.

spec.rawSql: SELECT round(100 * countIf(replaceRegexpAll(toString(SrcCountry), '\\x00', '') != '' OR replaceRegexpAll(toString(DstCountry), '\\x00', '') != '') / greatest(count(), 1)) AS pct FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND (SrcNetRole != 'internal' OR DstNetRole != 'internal')

spec.title: Countries Contacted
spec.description: Distinct destination countries resolved in this range. Counts only flows whose destination country actually resolved, so it is a floor on the real spread, not an estimate of it.

spec.rawSql: SELECT uniqExactIf(replaceRegexpAll(toString(DstCountry), '\\x00', ''), replaceRegexpAll(toString(DstCountry), '\\x00', '') != '') AS countries FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND DstNetRole != 'internal'

spec.title: Top Destination AS
spec.description: Networks your traffic actually goes to, by bytes. Requires GeoIP/ASN.

spec.rawSql: SELECT concat('AS', toString(DstAS), ' ', dictGetOrDefault('asns', 'name', toUInt64(DstAS), '')) AS asn, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS bytes FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND DstNetRole != 'internal' AND DstAS != 0 GROUP BY asn ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 15

spec.title: Top Source AS
spec.description: Internet-side source networks by bytes. This is the panel to inspect for inbound traffic or remote services sending data to the LAN.

spec.rawSql: SELECT concat('AS', toString(SrcAS), ' ', dictGetOrDefault('asns', 'name', toUInt64(SrcAS), '')) AS asn, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS bytes FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND SrcNetRole != 'internal' AND SrcAS != 0 GROUP BY asn ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 15

spec.title: Top Destination Country
spec.description: Destination countries by bytes. Requires GeoIP.

spec.rawSql: SELECT replaceRegexpAll(toString(DstCountry), '\\x00', '') AS country, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS bytes FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND DstNetRole != 'internal' AND replaceRegexpAll(toString(DstCountry), '\\x00', '') != '' GROUP BY country ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 15

spec.title: Top Source Country
spec.description: Internet-side source countries by bytes. Missing countries are stripped instead of showing ClickHouse FixedString NUL bytes.

spec.rawSql: SELECT replaceRegexpAll(toString(SrcCountry), '\\x00', '') AS country, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS bytes FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND SrcNetRole != 'internal' AND replaceRegexpAll(toString(SrcCountry), '\\x00', '') != '' GROUP BY country ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 15

spec.title: Throughput by Destination AS
spec.description: Bit rate to the eight busiest destination networks. Requires GeoIP/ASN.

spec.rawSql: SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeReceived) AS time, concat('AS', toString(DstAS)) AS asn, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) * 8 / $__interval_s AS bps FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND DstNetRole != 'internal' AND DstAS != 0 AND DstAS IN (SELECT DstAS FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND DstNetRole != 'internal' AND DstAS != 0 GROUP BY DstAS ORDER BY sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) DESC LIMIT 8) GROUP BY time, asn ORDER BY time

spec.title: Throughput by Source AS
spec.description: Bit rate from the eight busiest source networks. Useful for inbound traffic and remote services that send large responses.

spec.rawSql: SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeReceived) AS time, concat('AS', toString(SrcAS)) AS asn, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) * 8 / $__interval_s AS bps FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND SrcNetRole != 'internal' AND SrcAS != 0 AND SrcAS IN (SELECT SrcAS FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND SrcNetRole != 'internal' AND SrcAS != 0 GROUP BY SrcAS ORDER BY sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) DESC LIMIT 8) GROUP BY time, asn ORDER BY time

spec.title: AS Conversation Matrix
spec.description: Who is talking to whom at the AS level, with local or unresolved sides grouped as AS0. This makes CDN, resolver, cloud, and remote-service relationships visible in one sortable table.

spec.rawSql: SELECT concat('AS', toString(SrcAS), ' ', dictGetOrDefault('asns', 'name', toUInt64(SrcAS), '')) AS SourceAS, concat('AS', toString(DstAS), ' ', dictGetOrDefault('asns', 'name', toUInt64(DstAS), '')) AS DestinationAS, count() AS Flows, uniq(SrcAddr) AS Sources, uniq(DstAddr) AS Destinations, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS Bytes, sum(Packets * SamplingRate) AS Packets FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND (SrcAS != 0 OR DstAS != 0) GROUP BY SourceAS, DestinationAS ORDER BY Bytes DESC LIMIT 50

spec.title: Country Pair Matrix
spec.description: Country-to-country pairs after stripping missing FixedString values. This is a compact way to see where traffic is going without exposing individual IPs.

spec.rawSql: SELECT if(replaceRegexpAll(toString(SrcCountry), '\\x00', '') = '', 'unresolved', replaceRegexpAll(toString(SrcCountry), '\\x00', '')) AS SourceCountry, if(replaceRegexpAll(toString(DstCountry), '\\x00', '') = '', 'unresolved', replaceRegexpAll(toString(DstCountry), '\\x00', '')) AS DestinationCountry, count() AS Flows, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS Bytes FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND (SrcNetRole != 'internal' OR DstNetRole != 'internal') GROUP BY SourceCountry, DestinationCountry ORDER BY Bytes DESC LIMIT 50

spec.title: Where the Traffic Goes
spec.description:
Destination countries, marker size and colour by bytes.

Only flows whose destination country resolved appear here -- roughly a third of boundary-crossing flows, per the Country Resolution tile above. Read the map as 'where the identified traffic went', not as a complete picture: an absent country means unresolved just as often as it means unvisited.

Markers sit at country centroids from Grafana's built-in gazetteer. They are not the location of any actual host, and country-level GeoIP is itself only an approximation -- anycast CDN traffic in particular resolves to wherever the address block is registered.

spec.rawSql: SELECT replaceRegexpAll(toString(DstCountry), '\\x00', '') AS country, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS bytes FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND DstNetRole != 'internal' AND replaceRegexpAll(toString(DstCountry), '\\x00', '') != '' GROUP BY country ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 100

spec.title: Local Hosts to External Networks
spec.description:
Which local devices talk to which networks on the internet, sized by bytes. Node stats are bytes (main) and flow count (secondary).

Only flows with a resolved destination AS are included, and only the 60 heaviest host-to-network pairs in the range -- Grafana hides nodes past 200 behind cluster markers, so the cap keeps the graph readable rather than truthful-but-unusable. The dashboard keeps the grouped label set bounded for Grafana.

This is the same relationship the AS Conversation Matrix below states as a table. The table is what you sort and filter; this is what makes a device with an unexpected number of network relationships obvious at a glance.

spec.rawSql: WITH pairs AS (SELECT replaceRegexpAll(IPv6NumToString(SrcAddr), '^::ffff:', '') AS host, toString(DstAS) AS asn, dictGetOrDefault('asns', 'name', toUInt64(DstAS), concat('AS', toString(DstAS))) AS as_name, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS bytes, count() AS flows FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND SrcNetRole = 'internal' AND DstNetRole != 'internal' AND DstAS != 0 GROUP BY host, asn, as_name ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 60) SELECT concat('h:', host) AS id, host AS title, 'local host' AS subtitle, sum(bytes) AS mainstat, sum(flows) AS secondarystat FROM pairs GROUP BY id, title UNION ALL SELECT concat('a:', asn) AS id, as_name AS title, concat('AS', asn) AS subtitle, sum(bytes) AS mainstat, sum(flows) AS secondarystat FROM pairs GROUP BY id, title, subtitle

WITH pairs AS (SELECT replaceRegexpAll(IPv6NumToString(SrcAddr), '^::ffff:', '') AS host, toString(DstAS) AS asn, dictGetOrDefault('asns', 'name', toUInt64(DstAS), concat('AS', toString(DstAS))) AS as_name, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS bytes, count() AS flows FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND SrcNetRole = 'internal' AND DstNetRole != 'internal' AND DstAS != 0 GROUP BY host, asn, as_name ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 60) SELECT concat(host, '>', asn) AS id, concat('h:', host) AS source, concat('a:', asn) AS target, bytes AS mainstat, flows AS secondarystat FROM pairs

options.content:
## Shapes worth a second look
Nothing on this tab is an alert, and nothing here means you have been attacked. These are traffic *shapes* that are occasionally worth explaining -- and that a home network produces innocently all the time.

- A browser opening a page touches dozens of CDN endpoints; that is fan-out.
- Connections get reset constantly as pages are abandoned; that is resets.
- Phones and TVs probe the LAN continuously; that is discovery traffic.

The useful signal is almost never a single number being non-zero. It is a **change**: a device that suddenly fans out far wider than it used to, or a reset rate that climbs against one destination. Compare against a quiet period before drawing conclusions.

**Coverage caveat applies here more than anywhere else.** Hardware flow offload means softflowd never sees some traffic, so absence of a signal on this tab is not evidence of absence. Check the Pipeline Health tab first.

spec.title: Reset Rate
spec.description:
Share of TCP flows in which a RST was seen at any point.

A quarter to a third is entirely normal -- browsers abandon connections, servers close idle sockets, and connection racing (Happy Eyeballs) resets the loser by design. Watch the trend, not the value, and cross-check against the destination breakdown below if it moves.

spec.rawSql: SELECT round(100 * countIf(bitAnd(TCPFlags, 4) != 0) / greatest(count(), 1)) AS pct FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND Proto = 6

spec.title: Unanswered Attempts
spec.description:
TCP flows that carried a SYN and never a matching ACK -- a connection attempt that got nothing back.

This is the closest thing in the dataset to a scan signature, and it is normally a handful of flows: an unreachable host, a service that moved, a stale bookmark. It has no threshold colour on purpose, because the number that matters is how it compares to yesterday, not whether it crossed a line someone guessed at.

spec.rawSql: SELECT countIf(bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0 AND bitAnd(TCPFlags, 16) = 0) AS flows FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND Proto = 6

spec.title: Widest Fan-out
spec.description:
The largest number of distinct external addresses any single local host contacted in this range.

Ordinary web browsing reaches hundreds of endpoints per hour, so a high number is normal for a laptop or phone and notable for a device that should be quiet -- a thermostat, a printer, a camera. The table below names which host it was.

spec.rawSql: SELECT max(dests) AS dests FROM (SELECT uniq(DstAddr) AS dests FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND SrcNetRole = 'internal' AND DstNetRole != 'internal' GROUP BY SrcAddr)

spec.title: Inbound Sources
spec.description:
Distinct internet-side addresses that sent traffic to a well-known port (below 1024) on a local host.

Behind NAT with no port forwards this is mostly replies to things the LAN started -- NTP servers answering, for instance. A rising count, or traffic to a port you did not expose, is worth explaining.

spec.rawSql: SELECT uniq(SrcAddr) AS sources FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND SrcNetRole != 'internal' AND DstNetRole = 'internal' AND DstPort > 0 AND DstPort < 1024

spec.title: TCP Flow Outcomes over Time
spec.description:
The decoded TCP outcomes from the Applications tab, over time and stacked.

The point of the time axis is that the mix is normally stable. A step change -- resets suddenly dominating, or unanswered attempts appearing in a band where there were none -- is the thing to notice; the absolute counts follow whatever the network was doing.

spec.rawSql: SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeReceived) AS time, countIf(multiIf(bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0 AND bitAnd(TCPFlags, 16) = 0, 'SYN, never answered', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 4) != 0, 'RST - reset or refused', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 1) != 0 AND bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0, 'Completed - opened and closed', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 1) != 0, 'Closed - handshake not captured', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0, 'Open - handshake, still running', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 16) != 0, 'Established - data only', 'Other') = 'Completed - opened and closed') AS "Completed - opened and closed", countIf(multiIf(bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0 AND bitAnd(TCPFlags, 16) = 0, 'SYN, never answered', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 4) != 0, 'RST - reset or refused', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 1) != 0 AND bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0, 'Completed - opened and closed', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 1) != 0, 'Closed - handshake not captured', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0, 'Open - handshake, still running', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 16) != 0, 'Established - data only', 'Other') = 'RST - reset or refused') AS "RST - reset or refused", countIf(multiIf(bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0 AND bitAnd(TCPFlags, 16) = 0, 'SYN, never answered', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 4) != 0, 'RST - reset or refused', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 1) != 0 AND bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0, 'Completed - opened and closed', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 1) != 0, 'Closed - handshake not captured', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0, 'Open - handshake, still running', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 16) != 0, 'Established - data only', 'Other') = 'SYN, never answered') AS "SYN, never answered", countIf(multiIf(bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0 AND bitAnd(TCPFlags, 16) = 0, 'SYN, never answered', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 4) != 0, 'RST - reset or refused', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 1) != 0 AND bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0, 'Completed - opened and closed', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 1) != 0, 'Closed - handshake not captured', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0, 'Open - handshake, still running', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 16) != 0, 'Established - data only', 'Other') = 'Open - handshake, still running') AS "Open - handshake, still running", countIf(multiIf(bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0 AND bitAnd(TCPFlags, 16) = 0, 'SYN, never answered', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 4) != 0, 'RST - reset or refused', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 1) != 0 AND bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0, 'Completed - opened and closed', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 1) != 0, 'Closed - handshake not captured', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0, 'Open - handshake, still running', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 16) != 0, 'Established - data only', 'Other') = 'Established - data only') AS "Established - data only", countIf(multiIf(bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0 AND bitAnd(TCPFlags, 16) = 0, 'SYN, never answered', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 4) != 0, 'RST - reset or refused', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 1) != 0 AND bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0, 'Completed - opened and closed', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 1) != 0, 'Closed - handshake not captured', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0, 'Open - handshake, still running', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 16) != 0, 'Established - data only', 'Other') = 'Closed - handshake not captured') AS "Closed - handshake not captured", countIf(multiIf(bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0 AND bitAnd(TCPFlags, 16) = 0, 'SYN, never answered', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 4) != 0, 'RST - reset or refused', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 1) != 0 AND bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0, 'Completed - opened and closed', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 1) != 0, 'Closed - handshake not captured', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 2) != 0, 'Open - handshake, still running', bitAnd(TCPFlags, 16) != 0, 'Established - data only', 'Other') = 'Other') AS "Other" FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND Proto = 6 GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

spec.title: ICMP Volume
spec.description:
ICMP and ICMPv6 flow counts over time.

**No type/code breakdown is possible here.** ClickHouse ships an `icmp` dictionary that maps (protocol, type, code) to names like `echo-request` or `destination-unreachable`, but softflowd does not export ICMP type or code -- the field is a constant zero on every ICMP flow in this deployment. Decoding it would label everything `echo-reply`, which is what the dictionary returns for (1,0,0) and not a fact about the traffic. Volume is what the data honestly supports.

ICMPv6 is steady and high on any IPv6 LAN: neighbour discovery and router advertisement are ICMPv6. A sustained ICMPv4 climb is the more interesting of the two.

spec.rawSql: SELECT $__timeInterval(TimeReceived) AS time, countIf(Proto = 1) AS "ICMPv4", countIf(Proto = 58) AS "ICMPv6" FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND Proto IN (1, 58) GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

spec.title: Fan-out by Local Host
spec.description:
Local hosts ranked by how many distinct external destinations they contacted.

**This is a browsing-activity ranking as much as anything else.** A laptop at the top of this table is the expected result, not a finding. What is worth a look is a device with a narrow job -- a printer, a smart plug, an IP camera -- sitting anywhere near the top, or a host whose `Ports` count is high while its `Bytes` stay tiny, which is the shape of probing rather than of using a service.

`Networks` counts distinct destination ASes and is the steadier column: CDN fan-out inflates `Destinations` heavily but usually resolves to only a handful of networks.

spec.rawSql: SELECT replaceRegexpAll(IPv6NumToString(SrcAddr), '^::ffff:', '') AS Host, uniq(DstAddr) AS Destinations, uniq(DstAS) AS Networks, uniq(DstPort) AS Ports, count() AS Flows, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS Bytes FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND SrcNetRole = 'internal' AND DstNetRole != 'internal' GROUP BY Host ORDER BY Destinations DESC LIMIT 30

spec.title: Inbound to Local Hosts
spec.description:
Traffic from internet-side sources to well-known ports on local hosts.

Restricted to ports below 1024 to keep ordinary reply traffic on ephemeral ports out. Most of what remains is still solicited -- an NTP server answering the LAN's own query looks exactly like an inbound flow to port 123, because from the capture's point of view that is what it is. softflowd cannot tell a reply from an unsolicited connection.

Read it as an inventory of what reaches in and on which port, and check anything you did not deliberately expose. An empty table is the expected state behind NAT with no port forwards.

spec.rawSql: SELECT replaceRegexpAll(IPv6NumToString(DstAddr), '^::ffff:', '') AS Target, DstPort AS Port, dictGetOrDefault('protocols', 'name', toUInt64(Proto), toString(Proto)) AS Protocol, uniq(SrcAddr) AS Sources, count() AS Flows, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS Bytes FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) AND SrcNetRole != 'internal' AND DstNetRole = 'internal' AND DstPort > 0 AND DstPort < 1024 GROUP BY Target, Port, Protocol ORDER BY Flows DESC LIMIT 30

options.content:
## Is the flow data trustworthy?
Everything on this tab is Prometheus, not ClickHouse. The flow pipeline has three failure modes that produce *plausible but wrong* data rather than an error:

1. **Hardware flow offload** -- packets forwarded by the switch ASIC never reach softflowd.
2. **libpcap drops** -- the router could not keep up and flows are missing packets.
3. **Flow table overflow** -- `max_flows` was hit, so flows expired early and byte counts are truncated.

All three are surfaced below. Treat a non-zero value in any of them as 'the numbers on the other tabs are a lower bound'.

spec.title: Exporter Running
spec.description: Whether every configured softflowd instance answered on its control socket. Reads 0 if any capture interface has no live exporter.

spec.title: Flow Data Complete
spec.description: 0 means hardware flow offload is enabled, so the switch ASIC forwards traffic the CPU never sees and softflowd cannot capture it. Flow totals are then incomplete by an unknown amount. Set NETFLOW_DISABLE_HW_OFFLOAD=1 when running setup.sh to trade routing throughput for complete accounting.

spec.title: Capture Drops
spec.description: Packets libpcap discarded because softflowd could not keep up. Anything above zero means flows are missing packets; reduce the captured interface set or raise NETFLOW_SAMPLING_RATE.

spec.title: Forced Flow Expiry
spec.description: Flows expired early because the softflowd flow table was full. Non-zero truncates byte counts; raise NETFLOW_MAX_FLOWS.

spec.title: Router Exporter Rates
spec.description: softflowd's own counters. Export failures mean the router could not send to the collector -- check the inlet is reachable on the NetFlow port.

spec.title: Collector Pipeline Rates
spec.description:
Akvorado's own counters, scraped as job="akvorado". Two gaps to read here:

- **inlet kernel drops** above zero means the UDP receive buffer overflowed. Akvorado's docs are explicit that this makes byte and packet counts unreliable, because the reported sampling rate no longer matches what actually arrived.
- **received but not stored** means enrichment is dropping flows. Almost always an ifIndex that akvorado/exporters.yaml does not know. The breakdown panel below names the exact reason.

spec.title: Capture Interfaces and ifIndex
spec.description: The ifIndex column is what must match akvorado/exporters.yaml. A mismatch discards every flow from that interface with no error anywhere -- it looks identical to NetFlow not working at all.

spec.title: Flow Table Occupancy
spec.description: Flows currently tracked by softflowd. Approaching NETFLOW_MAX_FLOWS (8192 by default) is what causes the forced expiry above.

spec.title: Collector Available
spec.description: Whether the health collector itself ran and reached at least one exporter. 0 with the netflow profile installed means softflowctl is missing or every instance is down.

spec.title: Export Failures
spec.description: Flows softflowd could not send to the collector over the selected range. Non-zero means UDP to the Akvorado inlet is failing.

spec.title: Textfile Freshness
spec.description: Age of the router's textfile metrics, including this collector's output. A stale value means cron is not running the health script.

spec.title: Collector Error Reasons
spec.description: Why the outlet discarded flows over the selected range, by Akvorado's own reason label. 'metadata missing' means the ifIndex is not in akvorado/exporters.yaml - the most likely failure on a fresh install. 'sampling rate missing' is normal briefly at startup but should stop increasing; if it keeps climbing, akvorado.yaml's default-sampling-rate is not taking effect. Empty is the healthy state.

spec.title: Availability History
spec.description:
Each of the three trust conditions above, over the selected range instead of right now.

This is the panel that answers 'was it down at 3am'. A gap in **Exporter running** means softflowd was not answering, so flows from that window are missing entirely rather than merely incomplete. **Capture complete** going red means hardware flow offload was active and the totals for that period are a lower bound.

The three series are deliberately the same conditions as the tiles at the top of the tab, so a tile and its history can never disagree.

spec.title: Direction Cross-Check
spec.description:
Akvorado's own `FlowDirection` against the direction this dashboard derives from address role. These are independent signals and this table is the only place they meet.

The expected shape is a strong diagonal: `egress`/`outbound` and `ingress`/`inbound` should carry nearly all the flows. That agreement is what justifies using address role everywhere else -- `InIfBoundary` is unusable here because softflowd reports one ifIndex for both directions, but `FlowDirection` is populated independently and corroborates the workaround.

If the diagonal breaks down, suspect `clickhouse.networks` in akvorado.yaml: a LAN prefix missing from it makes every local address look external and skews every direction-split panel on the Flow Overview tab. Rows with a blank role are flows where neither side matched a configured prefix.

spec.rawSql: SELECT FlowDirection AS Reported, multiIf(SrcNetRole = 'internal' AND DstNetRole = 'internal', 'local', SrcNetRole = 'internal', 'outbound', 'inbound') AS Derived, count() AS Flows, sum(Bytes * SamplingRate) AS Bytes FROM flows WHERE $__timeFilter(TimeReceived) AND $__conditionalAll(ExporterName IN (${router:singlequote}), $router) GROUP BY Reported, Derived ORDER BY Flows DESC LIMIT 20

options.content:
## Where the collector is struggling
Akvorado's own pipeline, in order: **inlet** receives UDP and pushes to Kafka without parsing, **Kafka** buffers, **outlet** consumes, decodes, enriches, and batch-inserts into ClickHouse.

Walk it in that order when something is wrong -- the first stage that stops keeping up is the one to fix. Consumer lag rising while everything else looks fine means the outlet is the bottleneck; insert latency rising means ClickHouse is.

All of this is collector health, not flow data. A perfectly healthy pipeline still cannot recover traffic that hardware offload hid from softflowd in the first place -- that is the Pipeline Health tab's job.

spec.title: Kafka Consumer Lag
spec.description:
Messages sitting in Kafka that the outlet has not consumed yet.

Zero or near-zero is healthy and normal here. Sustained growth means the outlet cannot keep up with the inlet -- flows are not lost while Kafka still holds them, but they are arriving in ClickHouse late, so recent panels on the other tabs will read low until it catches up. If lag keeps climbing, the retention on the Kafka topic eventually decides what gets dropped.

The threshold band is a judgement call, not a measured limit: this deployment sits at zero, so anything into the thousands is a real change of state rather than noise.

spec.title: ClickHouse Insert Latency
spec.description:
How long each batch insert into ClickHouse takes, from Akvorado's own histogram.

`le` is preserved inside the inner aggregation, which `histogram_quantile` requires. Rising p95 with flat p50 is ClickHouse occasionally stalling -- usually merges or disk pressure; both percentiles rising together is sustained write pressure. This is the stage immediately upstream of every ClickHouse panel on this dashboard, so latency here shows up there as data arriving late.

spec.title: Decoder Throughput by Record Type
spec.description:
NetFlow records decoded per second, split by record type.

This panel exists for one specific failure that is otherwise invisible: **templates arriving with no data records**. NetFlow v9 sends the schema (`TemplateFlowSet`, `OptionsTemplateFlowSet`) separately from the data (`DataFlowSet`). If softflowd is running but capturing nothing, the template lines keep ticking along at their usual slow rate while `DataFlowSet` sits flat at zero -- the pipeline looks alive from every other angle and no flows arrive.

Healthy is `DataFlowSet` far above the rest. `DataFlowSet` at zero with templates still flowing means checking the capture interface and pcap filter on the router.

spec.title: Metadata Cache Hit Ratio
spec.description:
Share of interface-metadata lookups served from the outlet's cache.

The denominator is guarded with `> 0` so an idle or freshly-restarted outlet renders no data rather than `+Inf` or a misleading 100%.

This should sit very close to 1 in a single-router deployment: there is one exporter and one interface, so after the first lookup everything is a hit. A ratio that drops and stays down means entries are being evicted or expired faster than they are used, which is the same underlying condition that produces `metadata missing` errors on the Collector Error Reasons panel.

spec.title: Outlet Worker Load
spec.description:
How often the outlet's ClickHouse writer workers reported themselves steady, overloaded, or underloaded -- Akvorado's own autoscaling signal.

Sustained `overloaded` is the saturation warning that precedes consumer lag: the workers are asking for help before the backlog becomes visible upstream. `underloaded` dominating is the normal state on a home link and is not a problem to fix.

spec.title: Flows per ClickHouse Batch
spec.description:
How many flows the outlet packs into each ClickHouse insert.

This is a Prometheus **summary**, not a histogram -- it publishes precomputed quantiles under a `quantile` label and has no `le` buckets, so `histogram_quantile()` over it returns nothing. The quantiles are selected directly.

Read it together with insert latency: small batches with high latency means the outlet is flushing early under time pressure rather than filling batches, which is inefficient but not lossy. Batch size is driven by flow arrival rate, so it tracks how busy the network is.
